$comment: Lock file for vendored skills. Each entry is copied byte-for-byte from `repo`/`path` at `rev` (plus the upstream license and any `patches`, which only cut references to upstream skills the hub leaves out). tools/vendor.py keeps it honest; the weekly upstream-sync workflow proposes new revs as reviewable pull requests.

skills.name: brainstorming
skills.why: Classifies a request as spike, bounded or architectural and gets the design approved before any code; architectural work ends in a written spec for writing-plans. The optional visual companion starts a local Node server from scripts/ only after you accept it.

skills.name: writing-plans
skills.why: Turns an approved spec into a task-by-task plan with exact files, interfaces and failing tests, then hands off to subagent-driven-development or executing-plans.

skills.name: executing-plans
skills.why: Runs a writing-plans plan inline, task by task, with a ledger that survives compaction and one fresh review at the end. It calls subagent-driven-development's scripts and requesting-code-review's reviewer template, so both are vendored with it. Patched: drops a path into the using-superpowers bootstrap, which is not vendored.

skills.name: subagent-driven-development
skills.why: Runs a plan with a fresh implementer and task reviewer subagent per task; the executor writing-plans recommends. Owns the workspace, brief and review-package scripts that executing-plans also runs.

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.why: Red-green-refactor with a failure watched before any production code, plus rules against mock-only and mirror assertions. Patched: drops a pointer to writing-skills, which is not vendored.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.why: Root cause before any fix, in four phases; after three failed fixes it stops to question the design.

skills.name: verification-before-completion
skills.why: No success claim without a fresh command run and its output. A required sub-skill of executing-plans and systematic-debugging.

skills.name: requesting-code-review
skills.why: Dispatches a reviewer subagent on an exact commit range; its code-reviewer.md is the template both plan executors use for the final whole-branch review.

skills.name: using-git-worktrees
skills.why: Sets up an isolated workspace, preferring the harness's native worktree tool and any worktree directory your instructions declare. The setup step of both plan executors.

skills.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skills.why: Closes out a plan: full test run, then merge, PR or keep, and cleanup only of worktrees it created. The last step of both plan executors.
